articles.standfirst: 16ª edição do festival acontece de 20 a 29 de novembro, com produções de 60 países distribuídas em mostras especiais e competitivas e sessões ao ar livre.
articles.summary: 16ª edição do festival acontece de 20 a 29 de novembro, com produções de 60 países distribuídas em mostras especiais e competitivas e sessões ao ar livre. Exibições são gratuitas.
articles.body:
Festival Internacional de Animação de Pernambuco (Animage) — Foto: Victor Jucá/Divulgação

A 16ª edição do Festival Internacional de Animação de Pernambuco (Animage) acontece entre os dias 20 e 29 de novembro. Durante os dez dias de atividades, serão exibidos mais de 280 filmes em diversas salas de cinema do Recife . A programação completa está disponível na internet . Todas as sessões são gratuitas.

A grade do evento apresenta curtas e longas-metragens de 60 países em mostras competitivas e especiais e sessões infantis, além de encontros entre realizadores brasileiros e internacionais. Uma das novidades é a Mostra Parque, com sessões de cinema ao ar livre, em parques e praças da cidade.

Entre os locais públicos que participam da programação, estão:

Espaços culturais da cidade, como o Cinema São Luiz, o Cinema da Fundação Derby, o Cinema do Museu, o Teatro Luiz Mendonça e o Cinema da UFPE, também recebem sessões.

A abertura do festival está marcada para as 17h do dia 20 de novembro, no Cinema São Luiz, no bairro da Boa Vista, no Centro da cidade, com a animação francesa "Jim Queen". Além da exibição do filme, um dos diretores do longa, Marco Nguyen, participa de uma entrevista aberta ao público.

A edição deste ano também recebe a estreia da "Sessão Petrobras - Mostra Competitiva de Longas-Metragens", que reúne dez produções de diferentes países. O público também pode conferir cinco longas recentes e clássicos da animação, como "Persépolis", de Marjane Satrapi.

Filme 'Persépolis' é um dos longas de animação exibido no Animage 2026 — Foto: Reprodução/Divulgação

Uma das mostras aguardadas pelo público é a Erótica, com curtas dedicados ao tema da sexualidade. As sessões acontecem no dia 29 de novembro no Cinema da Fundação do Museu, no bairro de Casa Forte, na Zona Norte da cidade.

A Mostra Africana tem curadoria da artista pernambucana Kalor Pacheco e reúne produções de diferentes países do continente e de artistas africanos em diáspora. Já a Mostra Fleischer Cartoons é composta por nove curtas históricos dos estúdios responsáveis pela criação de personagens famosos, como Betty Boop.

O resultado das mostras competitivas será anunciado no último dia do festival. Os filmes disputam R$32 mil em premiações, distribuídos entre as categorias de Melhor Longa-Metragem, Melhor Curta-Metragem, Melhor Curta Brasileiro e Melhor Curta Infantil.

Além disso, a premiação contempla o Troféu Petrobras Escolha do Público e os prêmios ANIMAGE de melhor estudantil, direção, roteiro, direção de arte, técnica de animação e som.

O festival também realiza o ANIMAGE Conecta, uma iniciativa dedicada à formação e ao mercado audiovisual. A programação formativa conta com oficinas, rodada de negócios, conferências, debates e masterclasses.

Guarujá (SP) receberá duas atrações: o Festival Árabe Mil e Um Sabores e o Festival de Fatias de Bolo. — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Guarujá

Guarujá , no litoral de São Paulo, recebe entre esta sexta-feira (6) e domingo (8) o Festival Árabe Mil e Um Sabores e o Festival de Fatias de Bolo . Os dois eventos têm entrada gratuita e acontecem das 11h às 22h, na Praça Horácio Lafer, em frente à Praia da Enseada.

A programação reúne 45 barracas gastronômicas com pratos tradicionais de diferentes países do Oriente Médio, além de fatias de bolo de diversos sabores, vendidas a partir de R$ 33. O público também poderá acompanhar apresentações de danças tradicionais.

No mesmo espaço, o público também encontra o Festival de Fatias de Bolo, com porções de diferentes sabores e recheios.

Os preços começam em R$ 33. Entre as opções estão chocolate, cenoura, Ninho com Nutella, pistache, churros, prestígio, morango, Red Velvet e bolo de pudim.

O evento é pet friendly e permite a entrada de animais de estimação.

articles.title: Sophie Charlotte surfa na onda calma de 'Menino do Rio' com a guitarra de Pepeu Gomes em baixa voltagem | G1
articles.body:
Sophie Charlotte se junta a Pepeu Gomes em gravação de 'Menino do Rio' produzida por Kevin White e editada em single via Malibu Studios — Foto: Divulgação

♬ Atriz que vem ampliando a atuação como cantora, Sophie Charlotte reforça a discografia com a edição do single “Menino do Rio”, em rotação nos aplicativos de áudio desde a noite de ontem, quinta-feira, 5 de novembro.

No single, Sophie surfa na onda calma da composição de Caetano Veloso – canção lançada em 1979 em álbuns de Baby do Brasil e do próprio Caetano, mas projetada na voz de Baby como tema de abertura da novela “Água viva” (TV Globo, 1980) – em gravação feita com produção musical de Kevin White, o Keviin, dono do Malibu Studios, que também funciona como selo fonográfico.

Neste registro inédito de “Menino do Rio”, a guitarra habitualmente hendrixiana de Pepeu Gomes soa com toque suave, em sintonia com a maciez do canto de Sophie Charlotte e em voltagem bem menor do que a do arranjo da gravação da música por Baby do Brasil em 1979.

articles.title: 'Jimmy' star Jen Lilley says keeping Jesus at center of marriage helped through 'extremely difficult times'
articles.summary: Hallmark star Jen Lilley tells Fox News Digital how portraying Gloria Stewart in the biopic "Jimmy" reinforced her own marriage values rooted in faith.
articles.body: Hollywood has seen its fair share of high-profile breakups, but Jen Lilley says the secret to her nearly 20-year marriage has nothing to do with fame, fortune or romance. In an interview with Fox News Digital, the "Jimmy" star credited putting Jesus first with helping her and her husband get through some of life's most challenging moments. For Lilley, the secret isn't a Hollywood-approved relationship trick or a carefully guarded marriage formula. WILLIE ROBERTSON'S FAITH-BASED ADVICE THAT'S KEPT HIS 34-YEAR MARRIAGE TO WIFE KORIE STRONG "This is just something that I can say for me personally. You know, maybe it's not the secret for other people, but we both, we have a really strong faith," Lilley told Fox News Digital. "And I think that for us, keeping Jesus at the center of our marriage has really been what has gotten us through extremely difficult times," she said. WATCH: JEN LILLEY WON'T LET HOLLYWOOD GET IN THE WAY OF HER FAMILY Lilley said her commitment to faith also influences the roles she takes in Hollywood. CHRIS PRATT SAYS HIS FAITH WILL BE 'THE MOST IMPORTANT THING' THAT HE PASSES ON TO HIS KIDS While many actors chase the next big opportunity, Lilley says no role is worth sacrificing for her brood. "I think the values that I hold onto are actually common to most people, but I really value my family. I will make decisions based on the well-being of my own children and my marriage, even when sometimes it's not what I want," she said. "There have been times I've had to turn down a role or something because it just doesn't fit what I need in this season." "The values that I've carried are just really making sure that you're loving your family and your neighbor well," she added. Lilley married engineer Jason Wayne in 2007, and the couple share four children, including two sons adopted through foster care and two daughters. In her latest project, the actress portrays Gloria Stewart, the wife of Hollywood legend Jimmy Stewart, in the biopic "Jimmy." While preparing for the part, Lilley discovered a love story that went far beyond the glamour of Hollywood. TIM ALLEN REVEALS THE ONE THING THAT HAS SAVED HIS NEARLY 20-YEAR MARRIAGE TO JANE HAJDUK "I think what surprised me the most was just how much they enjoyed each other's company their entire lives," she told Fox News Digital. Jimmy Stewart, once dubbed Hollywood's eternal bachelor, found lasting love with Gloria, who brought two sons from a previous marriage into their relationship. Stewart adopted the boys, and the couple later welcomed two daughters together. But their marriage faced challenges that went far beyond Hollywood. Lilley said Stewart returned from serving in World War II with symptoms she described as consistent with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), at a time when the condition was not yet formally recognized under that name. She described Gloria as the actor's emotional anchor — someone who could navigate Hollywood's elite social circles but also provide a safe haven when the cameras stopped rolling. WATCH: JIMMY STEWART'S FINAL WISH STRIKES A CHORD WITH ACTRESS JEN LILLEY Lilley told Fox News Digital portraying Gloria also gave her a fresh perspective on what keeps a marriage standing when life gets messy — trust, laughter and having someone who feels like home. ‘CHARLIE’S ANGELS’ STAR JACLYN SMITH LIVED APART FROM HER HUSBAND FOR 17 YEARS DURING THEIR 35-YEAR LOVE STORY "I think what made their marriage really work was the fact that they did have so much trust with each other, and they had a lot of humor," she said. "I mean, I think that if you don't have a sense of humor, good luck getting through life. You know, life has a perfectly adequate way of knocking you back down often." The lesson hit close to home for Lilley, who said the Stewarts' relationship reinforced the importance of finding laughter even during difficult seasons and being a dependable source of comfort for a spouse. The Hallmark actress called playing Gloria Stewart a dream come true. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? articles.title: David Bisbal, un enamorado de la F1 y fanático de Fernando Alonso: “Me levanto a las tres de la mañana”
articles.standfirst: El intérprete almeriense desveló que lleva siguiendo este deporte desde hace 25 años
articles.summary: El intérprete almeriense desveló que lleva siguiendo este deporte desde hace 25 años
articles.body: David Bisbal se encuentra en plena gira por América Latina y Estados Unidos con el ‘Tour Eternos’, el cual llegará a nuestro país a principios del próximo año 2027. El intérprete sigue demostrando su talento, algo que ha plasmado en el disco que salió hace apenas un mes, ‘Eternos’. Sin embargo, en una entrevista reciente en el pódcast ‘ADN (Algunos diálogos necesarios)’, de Pedro Ruiz, confesó una pasión que le lleva acompañando desde hace mucho tiempo. El intérprete almeriense es fan y aficionado de la Fórmula 1 y de Fernando Alonso. En el citado espacio explicó su relación con el mundo del motor y con el piloto asturiano. El cantante de Almería recalcó que es “fanático” de la Fórmula 1 desde hace más de dos décadas: “Me encanta desde hace 25 años. Hemos ido a Austria… hemos ido a un montón de grandes premios y yo conozco a Fernando. Cada vez que estoy con él me causa más admiración y su entorno también”. Por su parte, el artista desveló que, pese a los GP en otros países que en España se emitían de madrugada o a deshoras, él siempre mantenía intacta su pasión por el deporte y por el piloto asturiano: “Fernando Alonso ha hecho que yo me levante a las tres de la mañana según en qué lugar yo me encuentre del planeta o que me quede hasta la una o dos de la mañana. Ya fuera entrenamientos libres o clasificación, lo que sea”. Por último, el pasado mes de septiembre, tanto él como Alonso estuvieron en Montmeló, lugar en el que el bicampeón del mundo le subió en su monoplaza de Aston Martin de la categoría GT como copiloto. Allí, junto a Rosanna Zanetti, su mujer, vivió de cerca cómo conducía el de Asturias y la magia de la F1.

articles.title: Historic Havilland Hall private estate goes on sale for £65m
articles.summary: The large estate in Guernsey has connections to Oscar winning actresses and marmalade magnates.
articles.body:
A mansion once home to lieutenant-governors, a marmalade magnate and family of Oscar-winning actresses has been put on the market for £65m.

Havilland Hall in Guernsey sits in about 80 acres of land, has six bedrooms, seven bathrooms, five reception rooms, an indoor pool and is being marketed as the island's largest private estate .

The property's nearly 200-year history includes periods owned by marmalade businessman William Keiller, while descendants of its original owner included Oscar-winning actresses Olivia de Havilland and Joan Fontaine.

Estate agents Savills said estates of this scale were "extraordinarily rare in the Channel Islands and it is likely to draw a global audience."

Built by Lieutenant-Colonel Thomas Fiott de Havilland between 1829 and 1830, it later served as the official residence of Guernsey's lieutenant-governors.

William Keiller, whose family created the first commercial Dundee marmalade brand, was among the estate's former owners.

The estate was bought in 1922 by Count Lothair Blücher von Wahlstatt, whose family traced its ancestry to the Prussian commander whose forces helped the Duke of Wellington defeat Napoleon at the Battle of Waterloo.

The estate also has a connection to the wider de Havilland dynasty, whose later generations included aviation pioneer Sir Geoffrey de Havilland and Olivia de Havilland and Joan Fontaine .

As well as the main house, the estate includes five guest cottages, staff accommodation, office space, converted farm buildings, a wine cellar and games room.

Phillippa Dalby-Welsh, head of Savills' country department, described Havilland Hall as a "pre-eminent Channel Island estate".

She said: "At its heart is a distinguished Regency villa, with great provenance, alongside beautiful gardens, a wide range of ancillary accommodation, leisure facilities and the infrastructure to support a business operation.

"Estates of this scale are extraordinarily rare in the Channel Islands and it is likely to draw a global audience."

Nick Paluch, head of Savills' Guernsey open market residential business, said: "This truly is a superb home and a once in a generation opportunity."

articles.title: How Akai and Moog are embracing vibe-coded mods
articles.summary: inMusic is making open-source MPCs, hackable Moog synths, and vibe-coder-friendly DJ decks.
articles.body: inMusic, the parent company of Akai, Moog, Native Instruments, and more, has decided to embrace the modding community. In an interview with The Verge, inMusic CEO Jack O’Donnell said, “We’re going to provide a toolbox to the community, we’re going to provide the inner workings of, say, an MPC or Sample so that people can do what they want.” That “toolbox” includes making the code for devices like the recently teased MPC Sample Key open source, but also offering developers an SDK to make modifications easier and lessen the risk of bricking your beloved sampler. While Akai is eager to see what the modding community cooks up, and has started seeding devices to developers ahead of the official release of the Sample Key, the company takes reliability seriously. O’Donnell said the company wants to “make sure that our official software is completely stable and good for an artist on stage.” He can’t have Fred Again going on stage and discovering his MPC is riddled with bugs. But he also wants people to feel comfortable tinkering. “We’ll try to give them a reset button,” he said so “They can experiment with it, and then not lose what they have.” The company is planning to make a big splash NAMM, the annual convention of music manufacturers in Anaheim, with Creator Lab, where it will let technically curious musicians get some hands-on time hacking 22 new products from across its brands. That includes products from Moog, that might not seem like a natural pairing for vibe coding because of its analog design. But O’Donnell thinks it can be, “if we open it up correctly.” That will involve building a platform for devs to work around the analog parts of the circuit. Other companies have also embraced the modding community. Erica Synths recently released the source code for its LXR-02 drum machine, Polyend open-sourced its line of Tracker grooveboxes, and Behringer has also announced a slew of open-source devices, including a $150 clone of the MPC One called Kick, a clone of the E-mu SP-1200, the Anima DJ controller, the Ignite sequencer, and the Polykeys 61 MIDI controller. The change in the industry has been quick and seismic. O’Donnell said of the need to provide developers tools for hacking inMusic’s products, “I can tell you it wasn’t on our task list five weeks ago. It just all of a sudden has to be on a task list now.” Of course, not everyone is thrilled. Elektron has expressed mixed feelings about the emergence of vibe-coded mods. The company banned linking to hacks and modified firmware from its official forums, though not discussing them generally, citing concerns about the possibility of damaging instruments. A statement posted on its forums says: “We would always warn against modifications to our firmware and/or machines that could brick them (potentially rendering them unusable), prevent future updates, affect warranty coverage.” While Elektron doesn’t want people posting links to hacked Digitone firmware on its forums, it’s not actively trying to thwart the modding community. The consensus is there’s no going back now that vibe coding has upended the music gear world, and trying to stand in the way would be a mistake. inMusic’s O’Donnell told the Verge, “you can try to wall them off, which is just a losing battle one … and so we want to embrace them.”

articles.title: Taylor Swift Called the ‘Fakest’ New York Knicks Fan by 2 of Team’s Players: ‘It’s a Little Performative’
articles.summary: "I'm gonna get some hate from the Swifties," Tyler Kolek acknowledged.
articles.body:
After drawing ire from disgruntled football fans in 2023 who felt she was present at too many games, Taylor Swift has managed to irk men in another sport for apparently attending too few. New York Knicks point guards Tyler Kolek and Miles "Deuce" McBride recently criticized the pop star as the "fakest" fan of the 2026 NBA champions, accusing her and other celebrity row visitors of being "performative."

In a clip from an NBA 2K TikTok livestream Deflected posted Thursday (Nov. 5), the two men fiddled with game controllers while debating who they believe is the least authentic celebrity Knicks fan. "Maybe Taylor Swift," Kolek said, to which McBride offered, "I would agree."

What defines a "fake" Knicks fan, in their eyes? "They just want to be seen at the game, they're not necessarily fans," Kolek noted. "I don't know if I've seen her at any other games. I'm gonna get some hate from the Swifties. I guess she's got a lot going on, so she can't come all the time. But it's a little performative."

"Swifties not gonna like that answer," McBride said with a laugh as the two players shouted out Ben Stiller and Tracy Morgan for showing up consistently at Knicks games. "Everybody else [but Swift] is usually solid."

In a statement, a spokesperson for the Knicks told Billboard , "Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization."

Billboard has reached out to Swift's rep for comment.

The 14-time Grammy winner was present at Game 4 of the NBA Finals, cheering on the Knicks alongside Mariska Hargitay and Este and Alana Haim in custom Knicks T-shirts. Before that, she also traveled with now-husband Travis Kelce to watch an away game against the Cleveland Cavaliers.

It's ironic that Swift — who, as Kolek generously pointed out, might've been a little busy this season, having been gearing up to release Billboard Hot 100 -topping song "I Knew It, I Knew You" for Toy Story 5 the same month of the NBA Finals, among other projects — is now getting flack for this reason. It wasn't long ago that football fans expressed upset over the amount that she was seen at NFL games when she first started showing up to support Kelce.

"I think we all know that if there's one thing that male sports fans want to see in their spaces and on their screens," Swift later sarcastically joked about the outrage in her 2025 cameo on New Heights , "it's more of me."

articles.title: Bill Paxton's son takes on Western role late father never got to play: 'I could literally hear my dad'
articles.summary: James Paxton steps into the Western role his late father Bill Paxton was cast in over 30 years ago, calling the film a "conduit" to connect with him.
articles.body: Bill Paxton's son, James Paxton, is carrying on his late father's legacy by taking on a Western role that the "Twister" star was originally set to play more than 30 years ago. In 1991, Bill was cast alongside Malcolm McDowell in the Western comedy drama "Last Train to Fortune," but the project stalled following original director Lindsay Anderson’s death in 1994. "Last Train to Fortune" spent decades trapped in development but efforts to revive the movie were gaining momentum again in 2017 when Bill unexpectedly died, leaving the role that would ultimately be played by James. During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, James, 32, opened up about how the project became a deeply personal way to reconnect with Bill, who passed away in February 2017 following heart surgery. 'DEADPOOL' STAR ROB DELANEY REVEALS HOW LOSING 2-YEAR-OLD SON CHANGED HIS APPROACH TO FAME "When you lose somebody, such a close loved one, you often look for ways to still connect to them," James said. "And that can take all manner of forms and paths and shapes," he continued. "For me, I recognized immediately that this was the kind of project that I could literally hear my dad in my head the whole time. You know, if I needed any guidance or any motivation, or I had any questions, I knew that he would kind of — he would be right there with me, and he'd be cheering me on for it." SYLVESTER STALLONE SCOFFS AT NEPOTISM CRITICS OVER DAUGHTER'S 'TULSA KING' ROLE: 'YOU IDIOT' "So I saw it as a way to — almost like a conduit to commune with him, wherever he is and may be," James added. "And there's something beautiful about following in those footsteps." James recalled that Bill had his own way of putting his son’s decision to follow him into acting in perspective. WATCH: BILL PAXTON'S SON SAYS HE COULD 'LITERALLY HEAR' LATE DAD WHILE TAKING ON HIS WESTERN ROLE "Dad had this metaphor about if this was 100 years ago, and we were a family of shoemakers or cobblers, my father before me was a shoemaker and his father before him, you'd probably go into the family business and become, hopefully, a good shoemaker," James said. "So I've always held that close." Before Bill's death, he had been working with McDowell and producer Brad Wyman on the "Last Train to Fortune's" revival with Adam Rifkin as director, but financing repeatedly prevented the project from moving forward. After Bill's death, Rifkin, Wyman and McDowell eventually approached James, who previously said that he hadn't even known about the film while his father was alive. According to Rifkin, the movie was finally able to secure financing once James signed on. Bringing the project to fruition also had personal significance for Adam, whose late mother, Michele Rifkin, penned the original script for a PBS screenwriting competition in 1986. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "It was always her son Adam's dream to bring the film to life," James said. James recalled that Michele had been unable to visit the set as she was bedridden in the hospital during the movie's production. However, the late screenwriter had the opportunity to see James and McDowell in costume when the duo FaceTimed her during filming. "She told us that when she saw us in costume it was like we had walked right out of her imagination up off the page and into the real world," he remembered. "And that was so touching, and it immediately made me think about my dad in that moment." "Michele passed away not long after that, and she got to see the finished film before it was released privately, which was amazing, but it made me think all the more about my dad," James said. "Because I know that he … would've wanted us to make this even if he was still around, if they had never got off the ground. He would have been like, ‘James, here, this is your role,’ and so that kind of really made me think of him in that moment in particular." SCOTT EASTWOOD CREDITS HIS FAMOUS FATHER'S WORK ETHIC FOR MAKING HIM AWARE OF 'BULLS---' IN THE FILM INDUSTRY Although James was stepping into a role once intended for his father, he said he knew Bill would have wanted him to find his own approach to the character. "It was totally important for me to create my own version just because I know what Dad would tell me," he said. "And it's tough for me because he was my best friend, so all I wanna do is talk about him and celebrate him, but he goes, 'You're your own actor. You've been studying this. You're a professional.'" "But I know that he always wanted me to make it my own, and he would be like, 'Don't hitch up on my wagon too much, you'll find it in yourself.' But he would just give me these great acting pieces of advice and wisdom. So I knew that he wouldn't want me to focus on that. He'd say, 'Focus on, it's the character's moment to live, it's Jedediah Dooley's moment to come to life.' So it's not James up there, it's not Bill up there, it's the character." While Bill encouraged his son to forge his own path as an actor, James recalled that his father was equally determined for his children to develop discipline in other areas of their lives. Along with James, Bill shared daughter Lydia with his wife, Louise Newbury. "He didn't love it when my sister and I would sleep in too late," James remembered. "He was a bit of a drill sergeant when it came to just getting up and doing something. So he would come in, and I became almost like — it was Pavlovian. As a kid, I became conditioned to hear his footsteps coming down the hall. And if I wasn't sitting up and out of my bed by the time he came in the room, he'd rip the sheets off of me, and he'd go, 'Rise and shine, you're burning daylight out here.'" "And he just put up the blinds, and it would just flood the room with blinding light and I would freak out a bit," James continued. "But he'd get me going, and so I — even in my half-asleep state — I could jolt awake when I'd hear him coming. Even on the weekends, if he was home, he'd be like, ‘Come on man, get up and do something.’ He wasn't controlling about what that was, but it was about motivating me not to just stay in bed." James recalled how Bill also wanted his son to have real-life experiences and not define himself solely through acting. WATCH: BILL PAXTON'S SON RECALLS 'DRILL SERGEANT' DAD RIPPING SHEETS OFF HIM FOR SLEEPING IN "I used to have a ton of all kinds of odd jobs," James recalled. "I worked in tons of restaurants. I apprenticed as a tile maker. I worked for UPS. I had a lot of really cool experiences. I scooped ice cream, that was my first job. And those were largely thanks to dad encouraging me to do that." Though James said Bill supported his acting ambitions, he recalled that his father tried to prepare him for the realities of working in Hollywood. "I would say he was probably more concerned with warning me about all of the pitfalls and the hardships that can fall," James said. "Even somebody as successful as he was in his career, he ran the gamut of every Hollywood experience and every disappointment. "And he always talked about it's the time between jobs where you really can suffer," he continued. "'The death of a thousand paper cuts.' he would call it. You have to find something that can buoy you between jobs, and you don't put your self-worth in it." "If anything, he was like, ‘Man if you want to do anything else like, even just as much as this, do that instead,’" James recalled. "He was like, ‘This is a hard thing’ and so if anything, he kind of gave me this extra chip on my shoulder because I was like, 'Well, I'm gonna go, and I'm going to book something and show him.'" James made his career breakthrough in the USA Network crime thriller drama "Eyewitness," which premiered in October 2016. While speaking with Fox News Digital, James recalled Bill's reaction when he landed the leading role of Lukas Waldenbeck in the series. "He almost couldn't believe it, but there was this huge sense of relief," James said. "And he called it a ‘real ticket to ride,' as in, it was his way of saying, 'This is a real opportunity. Now you go and show them and stuff. You've done the work to get here.'" "So that was really cool," he continued. "He saw that right before he passed, which was amazing." Since starring in "Eyewitness," James has steadily built his acting career with appearances in projects including "Training Day," "Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.," "Tacoma FD" and "The Cleaner." In 2024, he made a cameo in "Twisters," the standalone sequel to his father’s 1996 blockbuster "Twister." "I still get the whole 'it's Bill Paxton's son' thing, but I have over 45 acting credits," James told Fox News Digital. "But I laugh it off. As Dad would say, man it's all just — it's a great experience, and you're on the path." In "Last Train to Fortune," McDowell's character Cecil Peachtree misses the last train to his new teaching job in the frontier town of Fortune and enlists the help of James' Jedidiah Booley to get him there safely, with the mismatched pair forming an unlikely bond along the way. James told Fox News Digital that McDowell recently reminded him of a story that illustrated how the "Clockwork Orange" star's friendship with his father extended far beyond Hollywood. "I grew up in the Ojai Valley, and we've obviously been plagued by a lot of wildfires over the years," he said. "And it was a pretty bad one when I was quite young. articles.title: Kimmel says this recent Trump move is a sign he's 'planning to leave' soon
articles.summary: Jimmy Kimmel says Trump's recent moves suggest the president is "planning to leave" soon and calls his Oval Office updates "a skid mark."
articles.body:
Jimmy Kimmel has a new theory about President Donald Trump .

In his opening monologue on the Thursday, Nov. 5, episode of "Live," the late-night comedian said that after numerous Trump-backed Republican candidates lost in the recent midterm election, the president was preoccupied with the wrong thing.

Earlier that Thursday, Trump signed a proclamation to turn the Oval Office into a national monument , which Kimmel said was an effort to make sure "no future president can remove any of his crap."

The president has made headlines in recent months for his controversial White House renovations , which have homed in on a gold motif.

The host, 58, played a clip of Trump signing the document, saying, "I'm going to be signing a document, which will make them into a landmark for the ages. It won't be able to be taken down, destroyed, touched, or anything else."

Adam Carolla and Jimmy Kimmel from "The Man Show" appear on "The Tonight Show with Jay Leno" at the NBC Studios in Los Angeles on Nov. 19, 2001.

"That's right," Kimmel quipped. "His historic Diet Coke button will be preserved for many generations to come. I guess 'Tacky-o' really wants to make sure nobody lays a finger on all the beautiful new sconces and knickknacks he had spray-painted gold. He turned the Oval Office into the gift shop at the Liberace Museum."

Kimmel said the move signaled Trump was starting to make arrangements for his departure.

"Why do this now? Why do this right after the midterms?" Kimmel continued. "Maybe he's planning to leave sooner than we think?"

Kimmel called the new Oval Office a "landmark and a skid mark" and attempted to give Trump a reality check.

"Let me tell you something, buddy: On Jan. 20, 2029, we are gonna yank that crap down and throw it out faster than Melania moves back to New York," Kimmel said to cheers from the audience.

White House mocks Kimmel's 'peanut-sized brain'

In a statement to USA TODAY, White House spokesman Davis Ingle had brutal words for Kimmel.

"Jimmy Kimmel's case of Trump Derangement Syndrome is so advanced that it has completely rotted his peanut-sized brain," Ingle wrote. "He's far more entertaining when you're laughing at him than with him, but unfortunately his real talent is his failing ratings. This statement took more braincells to write than the average Jimmy Kimmel joke."

The comments follow Kimmel's remarks the day after midterms, in which the comedian said the president should leave office.

"Resign. Quit already," he said. "Just quit. Nobody wants you. Even you don't want to be president anymore."

articles.title: Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd reveal update on relationship status with honest message
articles.summary: Dallas Wings duo and Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd got honest while addressing the latest on their relationship status.
articles.body:
When the Dallas Wings drafted Azzi Fudd with the No. 1 pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft, it not only set the stage for a dynamic backcourt but also brought another unique storyline. Fudd and Wings star Paige Bueckers were rumored to be dating since their time together at UConn, and they'd share the floor again after leaving one of the nation's top college programs. However, as Bueckers clarified, the chatter about them dating when Fudd was drafted is apparently untrue.

Little has been heard about the duo since then, and while they meshed well during Fudd's first season in Dallas, it appears Fudd and Bueckers felt it was time to share an update. As they explained in a recent sit-down on Fudd's podcast Fudd Around and Find Out , they are no longer together, and both seemed completely at peace with it.

"Paige and I have something that we want to share with everyone," Fudd said. "We are no longer together."

Notably, Bueckers also addressed that they've been broken up for over a year and said they weren't together at the time of the 2026 WNBA Draft.

"Yeah, we're not together anymore. It's been, for everybody wondering....it's been a while." Bueckers said. "It's been like over a year. And [I wanted] to share that because everybody's going to be like, 'Oh my gosh, they're teammates, how is this going to work?'"

"We were not together before she got drafted, so all those narratives can go to bed. She was not drafted because she was my girlfriend," Bueckers continued. "She was drafted because she deserved it, and she's an amazing human. Amazing basketball player, and we're still friends; we're still cool. We broke up over a year ago, so we played an entire season together."

Bueckers followed up with an excellent, honest statement that she doesn't stand for hate of any kind, citing the negativity they've seen and felt around them.

"We don't stand for hate of any kind, like putting people down to lift us up, individually, together. Any negative nature of that kind, like we don't associate with that, we don't condone that," Bueckers said. "If you're using our names and our image to spread that, like, that's not who we are, and that's not what we're about."

"But if you support us, why would you hate on our teammates? Why would you hate on our friends?" Bueckers continued. "Why would you hate on our family? Like, why would you just tear people down to lift us up? That's never been something that we've stood for. So, to kind of address that, because we've seen a lot of negativity, we've seen a lot of hate. We've had stuff sent to us; we've had stuff sent to our family, our friends. And I hate that we have to address this, but just to control the narrative, there's been some crazy things said about us."

It's about as honest and candid a statement as one can make, and it's clear there have been off-court issues lingering around the duo and even their team, which is both terrible and disappointing. Kudos to Bueckers for her comments and for addressing the topic directly.

articles.title: Alec Baldwin not a fan of documentary about aftermath of ‘Rust’ shooting
articles.summary: The actor took part in the project, saying at the beginning of the film, “The worst thing for me is to be misunderstood.”
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — The people behind a documentary about Alec Baldwin on the aftermath of the “Rust” shooting say the movie’s subject isn’t a fan of the project.

Director Rory Kennedy and writer Mark Bailey attended a panel at the SCAD Savannah Film Festival following a screening of their documentary “The Trial of Alex Baldwin” last month.

“He really, really, really didn’t like it,” Kennedy said of Baldwin’s thoughts about the documentary, according to The Hollywood Reporter .

The actor took part in the project, saying at the beginning of the film, “The worst thing for me is to be misunderstood.”

“I think part of our experience was that Alec wasn’t always the most reliable narrator of himself. … So, part of what we’re trying to do, because we have these questions as filmmakers — when is he acting, what is real, what is not — we want to bring the audience into those questions as well so that it’s not like we’re presenting this as here’s all the facts,” Kennedy said at the film festival.

The documentary dives into Baldwin’s public persona, which has generated numerous headlines and a feud with the president , which frames it as a reason why he was put on trial.

The director continued, “Our feeling at the end of the day is you can feel what you might about Alec — and people have, often, strong feelings one way or the other — and you may still have those feelings at the end of the film that you had going into it, but I think most people, in watching the film, will feel like there was an injustice.”

In October 2021, during a rehearsal for “Rust,” Baldwin used a gun meant to be loaded with dummy rounds when he allegedly pointed it at the camera and fired, killing cinematographer Halyna Hutchins and wounding director Joel Souza.

The “It’s Complicated” actor, a producer on the film, claimed he didn’t pull the trigger and that it was fired accidentally.

Baldwin was charged with involuntary manslaughter in relation to Hutchins’ death, but a judge dismissed the case against the actor with prejudice in 2024.

In April, a Los Angeles Superior Court judge cleared the way for a civil trial to be brought against Baldwin stemming from the shooting.

articles.title: Taylor Swift is the ‘fakest’ celeb Knicks fan, players say; team rushes to her defense
articles.summary: The New York Knicks rushed to Taylor Swift’s defense Friday after players Tyler Kolek and Miles McBride questioned the singer’s fandom.
articles.body: The New York Knicks rushed to Taylor Swift’s defense Friday after players Tyler Kolek and Miles McBride questioned the singer’s fandom. The defending world champions were quick to jump on their white horse and laud the singer in the wake of their players stirring up some bad blood with blue-and-orange Swifties. “Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization,” a Knicks spokesperson said in a statement to NBC News. Kolek might even have some explaining to do to his girlfriend and self-identified Swiftie, Alexi Sousa, who wanted to know “what he had to say about my girl.” The Knicks famously boast a front row of world-famous fans at their Madison Square Garden home dates. When Kolek and McBride appeared on an NBA 2K TikTok livestream on Thursday and were asked who is “the fakest celeb fan you’ve seen courtside,” they dared to come for the 5-foot-10 Pennsylvania native and 14-time Grammy winner. “Maybe Taylor Swift?” Kolek said. “I don’t know if I’ve seen her at any other games.” McBride agreed, but acknowledged that he and Kolek had damaged their reputation and were headed for antihero status. “I would agree,” McBride said. “Swifties [are] not going like that answer.” Sensing he was in trouble, Kolek tried to backtrack and say Swift’s life as showgirl might make attending Knicks games a challenge. “I guess she’s got a lot going on so she can’t come all the time,” Kolek said. “But it’s a little performative.” Swift’s role in Knicks history will live as long as fans remember Game 4 of the NBA finals, when she sat courtside with Alana Haim, Este Haim and Mariska Hargitay at Madison Square Garden. They donned T-shirts with Knicks-ian puns and watched New York shake off a 29-point deficit to beat San Antonio. The Knicks, three days later, clinched the series in San Antonio and brought the NBA title back to New York for the first time since 1973. Swift is no stranger to the Knicks, as she famously visited practice in 2014 and got a lift from Amar’e Stoudemire for a memorable slam dunk.

articles.title: Ajulliacosta: do rap de Mogi ao Afropunk e indicação ao Grammy | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantora vê no festival um espaço de identificação e liberdade para pessoas negras. Evento acontece nos dias 7 e 8 de novembro, no Parque de Exposições Salvador.
articles.summary: Cantora vê no festival um espaço de identificação e liberdade para pessoas negras. Evento acontece nos dias 7 e 8 de novembro, no Parque de Exposições Salvador.
articles.body:
Aos 14 anos, enquanto escrevia em um caderno em Mogi das Cruzes , na Grande São Paulo, a rapper Ajulliacosta não imaginava que, aos 28, estaria subindo pela segunda vez no palco do Afropunk Brasil . O evento é considerado o maior festival de cultura negra do mundo e acontece nos dias 7 e 8 de novembro, no Parque de Exposições Salvador .

A volta da cantora ao festival, três anos após sua primeira apresentação, acontece em um momento de maior amadurecimento. "Eu volto com mais maturidade, eu volto até com uma certa gratidão pelo festival, porque, a partir dele, me abriu muitas portas", disse em entrevista ao g1 .

A preparação envolve diferentes elementos da apresentação, como balé, figurinos, estrutura de palco e participações especiais. A artista preferiu não revelar detalhes sobre as surpresas previstas para o show, mas afirmou que trabalha para transformar a apresentação em uma experiência especial tanto para o público quanto para a própria trajetória.

Ajulliacosta celebra raízes no rap, destaca força do AFROPUNK Brasil e se prepara para o Grammy Latino — Foto: Divulgação

A relação com o festival, no entanto, vai além da oportunidade de cantar em um grande evento. Para a rapper, o Afropunk tem um papel importante ao criar um ambiente em que artistas negros podem ser reconhecidos a partir de referências culturais e de uma sensibilidade que nem sempre encontram em outros espaços.

"Só a gente para olhar para a gente com tanta sensibilidade".

Para Aju, como é carinhosamente chamada pelos fãs, a identificação entre artistas e público é uma das características centrais do festival, que celebra seus corpos, suas estéticas e suas referências sem precisar se adaptar a padrões externos. A rapper ainda destaca que a moda, a música e as diferentes expressões individuais se encontram e formam um movimento coletivo de pertencimento.

"É um momento onde a gente se sente à vontade, onde a gente pode ser livre com o nosso corpo, com a nossa estética. É onde a moda tá muito presente também e cada um vai trazendo a sua referência, sabe? E ali cria um grande movimento", explicou.

Outro ponto destacado pela paulista foi o fato dos palcos serem lado a lado. "[Em 2023] Eu cantei em um palco que era igual ao de Alcione, que ficava ao lado do de Alcione. Não tem esse lugar de diminuir o artista. [A organização] Coloca a gente em uma régua de igualdade só por tá fomentando e continuando aquilo que os outros fizeram", enfatizou.

Ajulliacosta concorre ao Grammy Latino com o álbum “Novo Testamento” — Foto: Divulgação/Michelle Gomes

A música sempre esteve presente na vida de Ajulliacosta, mas foi a partir da escrita que a artista descobriu o próprio espaço no rap. Ainda adolescente, ela costumava registrar ideias em um caderno, sem imaginar que aquelas palavras poderiam ultrapassar o papel e ganhar o mundo.

Na época, com apenas 14 anos, a cantora acreditava que escrever era algo comum, sem perceber que aquela capacidade poderia ser um diferencial. Foi o contato com outros artistas e o reconhecimento de pessoas próximas que a ajudaram a entender que havia espaço para sua voz na música.

"Eu não só escrevo, eu também sou boa no que eu escrevo".

A trajetória construída desde então ganhou novos capítulos com o retorno ao Afropunk Brasil e a indicação ao Grammy Latino. Para a cantora, os dois acontecimentos representam oportunidades de ampliar o alcance do próprio trabalho, mas também de reafirmar os valores que orientam sua relação com o rap.

Ajulliacosta foi indicada ao Grammy Latino — Foto: Divulgação

Poucos dias depois do festival, Ajulliacosta tem outro compromisso importante: participar do Grammy Latino . A indicação foi recebida com surpresa pela artista, que concorre com o "Novo Testamento" (2025) na categoria Melhor Álbum de Música Urbana em Língua Portuguesa . "Foi uma delícia ser indicada ao Grammy, foi bom demais", contou.

A expectativa de conquistar o troféu existe, claro, mas ela também considera importante aproveitar o processo como parte de sua formação e de sua trajetória profissional.

"É lógico que a gente quer trazer o Grammy para casa. Está todo mundo tipo: 'Vamos trazer, vamos buscar'. Mas, de qualquer forma, eu vou viver esse momento".

A indicação representa mais um marco para a carreira da jovem. Da cena de rap de Mogi das Cruzes a uma premiação internacional, o percurso da cantora passou pelo reconhecimento de seu trabalho, pela ocupação de novos espaços e pela preservação de uma identidade artística ligada ao rap.

Além da carreira musical, Ajulliacosta também administra a AjcShop , uma marca de roupas autoral conectada à cultura hip-hop, à estética preta e à valorização de diferentes corpos e identidades.

Conciliar as duas atividades tem exigido mudanças na maneira como ela trabalha, sobretudo por precisar dividir responsabilidades e confiar processos a outras pessoas.

Durante muito tempo, a artista procurou acompanhar de perto todas as etapas dos projetos:

no negócio, participava de tarefas como costura e atendimento às clientes;

na música, também gostava de estar envolvida diretamente em tudo o que acontecia.

Com o crescimento das atividades, porém, ela percebeu que não seria possível manter o mesmo nível de participação em cada detalhe.

"Para mim, o aprendizado mais difícil é que não ia dar para dar conta de tudo".

O desafio, segundo a cantora, está relacionado ao apego aos próprios processos e à dificuldade de delegar tarefas quando se tem uma visão específica de como algo deve ser feito. Ao mesmo tempo, ela passou a reconhecer que outras pessoas podem contribuir com soluções diferentes e igualmente boas.

A experiência de liderança, dessa forma, também se tornou um processo de aprendizado, já que dividir responsabilidades não significa abandonar o controle sobre a própria trajetória, mas criar condições para que os projetos continuem crescendo sem depender exclusivamente de uma pessoa.

'O que a Julia quer? O que a Julia vai ser?'

Ajulliacosta fala sobre legado no rap — Foto: Divulgação

Quando pensa na maneira como gostaria de ser lembrada, Ajulliacosta destaca aquilo que pretende construir para a música brasileira. A cantora deseja ser reconhecida como uma artista que ocupou os espaços que considerava possíveis e necessários , sem se limitar às barreiras impostas ao longo do caminho.

Um dos pontos centrais dessa visão é a relação com o rap. Para ela, o crescimento profissional não deve significar o afastamento das referências que ajudaram a formar sua identidade.

"Eu acho que o rap me formou como ser humano, então ele tem que estar nas minhas atitudes também, nas coisas que eu vou trazer para o mundo".

A preocupação da artista vai além da continuidade de um gênero musical em seu repertório. O maior desejo dela é colaborar para que o rap continue em transformação e mantenha sua força.

Ao olhar para a própria história, Ajulliacosta reúne diferentes dimensões da experiência artística: a escrita que começou em um caderno, o apoio de quem reconheceu seu talento, a construção de uma carreira, os desafios do empreendedorismo e a chegada a palcos de projeção internacional.

O que conecta esses momentos é justamente a intenção de crescer sem romper com as próprias origens. Para a cantora, ocupar novos espaços não precisa significar deixar para trás aquilo que a formou, pelo contrário: é a partir dessa identidade que ela pretende seguir construindo seu lugar na música brasileira.

articles.title: Reeleita, Celina Leão terá desafio de reativar fomento à cultura, fortalecer FAC e bibliotecas no DF | G1
articles.standfirst: Governadora enfrentou críticas e problemas com o setor cultural em 2026; bloqueio de recursos foi a tônica. Nome para comandar a Secretaria de Cultura ainda não foi definido.
articles.summary: Governadora enfrentou críticas e problemas com o setor cultural em 2026; bloqueio de recursos foi a tônica. Nome para comandar a Secretaria de Cultura ainda não foi definido.
articles.body:
A relação do governo do Distrito Federal com o setor cultural, em 2026, foi marcada até aqui por uma sequência de críticas e problemas graves de subfinanciamento, adiamentos e pressões.

Desde que Celina Leão (PP) assumiu a chefia do Executivo local, os episódios se acumularam: impasses com o Fundo de Apoio à Cultura, atraso nos repasses ao Cine Brasília e o quase cancelamento do 59º Festival de Cinema.

Reeleita pelos próximos quatro anos, Celina afirmou ao g1 que pretende " intensificar as políticas culturais em todas as regiões do DF, fortalecer o Fundo de Apoio à Cultura e as bibliotecas da capital ".

Celina Leão (PP), governadora do DF — Foto: Divulgação

➡️Esta reportagem é a quinta (e última) de uma série sobre os desafios de Celina Leão para o próximo mandato .

➡️Na terça (3), o g1 mostrou os desafios de Celina na saúde pública . Na quarta (4), os desafios nas contas públicas e na gestão do BRB . Na quinta (5), os desafios na relação com o governo Lula . E na sexta (6), os desafios na educação .

Em 30 de março, logo após tomar posse, Celina Leão anunciou o cancelamento da festa de aniversário de Brasília . O orçamento de R$ 25 milhões que seria usado na comemoração foi destinado à Secretaria de Saúde, e a governadora avaliou a situação como "escassez de recurso".

"Eu sentei com o secretário de Saúde, e nós remanejamos esse orçamento para contratação imediata de médicos para a atenção básica. Tenho certeza que a população do DF sabe a importância desse gesto", afirmou na época.

Em agosto de 2026, um aviso publicado no Diário Oficial do Distrito Federal (DODF) confirmou a suspensão do Edital nº 06/2026 – FAC I/2026 – Demais Áreas, destinado à seleção de projetos artísticos e culturais para receber apoio financeiro do Fundo de Apoio à Cultura (FAC).

Segundo o documento, o edital foi suspenso por falta de orçamento para contratar os pareceristas – os técnicos que analisariam o mérito cultural de cada projeto. O custo era estimado em R$ 992,7 mil .

Na época, o governo afirmou que o problema era temporário, e que o edital seria retomado quando houvesse dinheiro em caixa, o que aconteceu em setembro .

Ainda em agosto, o GDF chegou a cancelar a realização da edição de 2026 do Festival de Brasília do Cinema Brasileiro , o mais antigo festival de cinema do Brasil, por falta de verbas.

No entanto, dias depois e após forte pressão dos setores, o governo voltou atrás e efetivou o pagamento da primeira parcela dos recursos para o evento . O festival aconteceu em setembro.

Segundo Celina Leão, "ainda não há um nome definido" para o comando da Secretaria de Cultura e Economia Criativa do Distrito Federal.

No entanto, a governadora já prevê algumas ações para os próximos anos.

"A partir de 2027, vamos intensificar as políticas culturais em todas as regiões do DF, fortalecer o Fundo de Apoio à Cultura e nossas bibliotecas. Também tenho o compromisso de entregar o Teatro Nacional Cláudio Santoro totalmente reformado à população", diz Celina.

Sobre as crises da pasta em 2026, a governadora diz que entende a preocupação dos profissionais do setor e quer definir prioridades para a área.

"Cultura, para mim, é identidade. É o que dá alma à nossa cidade e também gera trabalho e renda. Entendo a preocupação do setor com os cortes e quero manter o diálogo com artistas e produtores para definir prioridades e ampliar as oportunidades. Queremos abrir mais portas para quem vive de arte, com crédito, apoio à formalização e um novo polo de economia criativa no Setor Comercial Sul", afirma.

articles.title: 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend': Sharad Kelkar calls Yash's Ravana role his toughest; says, 'Dubbing for him was not at all easy'
articles.summary: Sharad Kelkar has opened up about dubbing for Yash, who portrays Ravana in Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana'.
articles.body: Sharad Kelkar has opened up about dubbing for Yash, who portrays Ravana in Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana'. The actor has provided the voice for Yash's character in the Hindi version. He recently discussed the challenges of the assignment, his conversations with Yash and the director's approach to portraying the demon king. Kelkar also praised Yash's preparation and identified several sequences that particularly impressed him.In an interview with Variety India, Sharad Kelkar revealed that Nitesh Tiwari and the film's core team approached him for the Hindi dubbing assignment. The actor said he had expressed his desire to work with the filmmaker during an earlier meeting. The opportunity eventually brought them together on the ambitious mythological project.Sharad Kelkar says Nitesh Tiwari's team chose him for YashSharad Kelkar recalled how the collaboration came about and mentioned his connection with Niraj Sanghai of Prime Focus. He also remembered meeting Nitesh Tiwari at Ravie Dubey's residence while the director was preparing for 'Ramayana'."Nitesh Tiwari and the core team decided that I should dub for Yash in the Hindi version. Niraj Sanghai of Prime Focus is a good friend. In fact, when I met Nitesh Sir last year at Ravie Dubey's place, I told him I wanted to work with him. He was busy preparing for the ‘Ramayana’ shoot. This was a great opportunity and finally, we worked together.”'Ramayana' explores Ravana's rise as an evil forceThe actor also explained how Nitesh Tiwari envisioned Ravana's journey in the film. According to Sharad Kelkar, the narrative gives considerable attention to the character's earlier life. It explores his origins and the events that shaped his transformation into an evil force."Nitesh Sir conceived the film basically from Ravan's rise as an evil force. While audiences have seen Lord Ram's childhood, nobody has seen Ravan's past: where he came from and what happened to him. Ravaan’s life is shown in a much extended manner than scenes from Ayodhya,” he said.Sharad Kelkar explains the challenges of dubbing for YashAlthough Sharad Kelkar praised Yash's portrayal of Ravana, he admitted that adapting the performance for Hindi audiences required considerable effort. Yash speaks Hindi well, but his Kannada-speaking background influenced certain aspects of his pronunciation and dialogue rhythm. The team therefore felt that a separate Hindi voice would work better for the character.“Yash has given an outstanding performance. He is the best choice for the role and he understood the character perfectly. Dubbing for him was not at all easy. I would describe it as interesting because Yash speaks Hindi quite well. But as someone who speaks mostly in Kannada, he has an accent and his rhythm with Hindi words was a bit of an issue. The entire team felt his voice needed to be dubbed for the Hindi version. In Kannada, he has done a brilliant job. He has a fantastic voice.”Yash and Sharad Kelkar worked closely during dubbingSharad Kelkar described Yash as approachable and actively involved in refining the Hindi version. Their conversations helped them work towards the desired outcome. The actor said Yash regularly offered suggestions and encouraged him to improve certain scenes.“Yash is a sweet guy. We had long chats and he would come up with suggestions. He was always striving for the best outcome asking me if I could better some of the scenes. We were all in sync."Sharad Kelkar reveals his favorite Ravana sequencesThe dubbing assignment was particularly demanding for Sharad Kelkar. He praised Yash's effort and described Ravana as one of the most challenging characters in the actor's career. Among his favorite moments were the ten-head sequence, the Vidyutjihva scene and the opening sequence involving Ravana seeking boons from Brahma.“It was one of my most tiring dubbing experiences. I cannot imagine how much effort Yash put in to ace this role. I feel this is the toughest role of his career and he has done an outstanding job. There are a couple of scenes conceived by Nitesh Sir, which I absolutely love. One of them is the 10 heads scene, then the Vidyutjihva one and the opening one where he seeks all the boons from Brahma.”Kelkar added that Ravana's intelligence and authority influenced his approach to the dubbing. He wanted the character to sound confident rather than uncertain, except in the scene where Ravana consults his ten heads about going to war.“Ravan is a very intelligent, well-read man and he has a command on things. While dubbing, I had to keep in mind that he cannot come across as confused or doubtful. articles.body:
After weeks of wondering who could be up for the mystery James Bond screen test, Deadline has not only found out who the actor is, another suitor was also added to the mix.

While not confirmed, insiders tell Deadline that Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult joined Jack Lowden, Josh O'Connor and Callum Turner in recent screen tests to play the next 007. While it was recently reported that four actors tested, insiders say a fifth test was added at the 11th hour (though it is unknown which actor was that last addition).

Amazon could not be reached for comment.

Deadline hinted at who the potential suitors were earlier this afternoon with confirmations coming tonight:

The process to find the next 007 goes back to the spring, when the studio announced casting director Nina Gold was joining the project and that the search was underway. Following two months of meetings, Deadline reported the first round of auditions would take place in August; since then, the studio, producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman and director Denis Villeneuve cut the list to its final group and worked out test offers in September.

The final tests were originally planned for earlier in October, but due to scheduling conflicts with the finalists, were pushed to the end of the month so they could happen around the same time. While not confirmed, sources say the group was no bigger than five actors, with Turner and O'Connor among the others who would end up testing.

It is unknown when the decision will be made, though most believe it will come by the end of the month and potentially before Thanksgiving. Stay Tuned.

articles.title: 'Nobody forces actors without consent': 'Mookuthi Amman 2' actor Ineya on intimate scenes in movies, feels performers must speak up
articles.summary: Actress Ineya spoke about consent and personal boundaries in the film industry, saying performers must communicate their discomfort before agreeing to
articles.body: Actress Ineya spoke about consent and personal boundaries in the film industry, saying performers must communicate their discomfort before agreeing to scenes they do not wish to do. She believes nobody can force an actor to perform something against their will. According to her, problems arise when people hesitate to express their concerns at the appropriate time.In an interview with Movie World Media, Ineya discussed intimate scenes, revealing costumes and the importance of setting boundaries during film shoots. She said actors should clearly explain their reservations if they are uncomfortable with particular requirements. The actress also argued that raising objections only after agreeing to something serves no purpose.Iniya says actors must communicate their discomfortSpeaking about consent on film sets, Ineya said performers have the freedom to refuse scenes that make them uncomfortable. She specifically mentioned intimate sequences, bedroom scenes, kissing and hugging. The actress also referred to revealing costumes as something performers should be able to decline if they are not comfortable wearing them."In the film industry, nobody forces us to do anything. Nobody can make us do something without our consent. If I am not comfortable doing intimate scenes, bedroom scenes, kissing scenes or hugging scenes, I should say so. I should also make it clear if I am uncomfortable wearing revealing clothes. Once I communicate that, if the scene requires it, the filmmakers can use cinematic techniques to shoot it. If I agree to everything and go along with everything, there is no point later claiming that someone misused me or did something without my consent," Ineya said. Ineya recalls her father's advice about privacyThe actress also shared an analogy her father often uses to explain personal boundaries. Comparing a person's private space to a locked room, she said individuals must decide who they allow into their personal space."My father always tells me that my room is my private space. If someone has to enter my room by opening the door, they can do so only if I unlock it. Once that person comes inside and sits next to me, if I give them an opportunity to touch me or do something inappropriate, there is no point later complaining that they did this or that to me. I should know where to draw the line before unlocking the door and allowing someone in. There is no point saying afterwards that something like this or that happened to me," Iniya added.On the work front, Ineya is part of the ensemble cast of the Tamil fantasy-comedy film 'Mookuthi Amman 2', which stars Nayanthara in the lead role. articles.summary: Sunita Ahuja has shared an emotional account of how Diwali celebrations have changed in her household over the years.
articles.body: Sunita Ahuja has shared an emotional account of how Diwali celebrations have changed in her household over the years. Recalling the family gatherings that once made the festival lively, she said her home now feels considerably quieter. Her comments have attracted attention amid ongoing speculation about her relationship with husband Govinda.In a chat with Pinkvilla, Sunita spoke about missing the atmosphere of earlier celebrations. She remembered a time when relatives, children and her mother-in-law would come together at home. However, changing family circumstances have altered those traditions. Her mother-in-law has passed away, while the children have grown older and become busy with their individual lives.Sunita Ahuja says her home feels 'soona-soona' during DiwaliSunita said the house was once filled with activity during the festival. The presence of family members brought a sense of togetherness that she now misses. She also acknowledged that she cannot expect her grown-up children to remain at home just for the occasion."Pehle jab Diwali hoti thi, toh mera ghar bhara-bhara rehta tha. Ghar mein saas hoti thi, bhanje aur bachche hote the. Khoob chahal-pahal rehti thi, lekin ab bachche bade ho gaye hain aur saas bhi nahi hain. Isliye ab ghar soona-soona lagta hai. Main bachchon se yeh nahi keh sakti ki tum ghar par hi raho. Sabhi apni-apni zindagi mein vyast hain aur aap kisi ko disturb bhi nahi kar sakte." ("Earlier, during Diwali, my house would be full of people. My mother-in-law, nephews and children would all be there. The house would be buzzing with activity. But now, the children have grown up, and my mother-in-law is no longer with us. That's why the house feels so empty. I cannot tell the children to stay home just for me. Everyone is busy with their own lives, and you cannot disturb anyone either.")How Sunita Ahuja celebrates Diwali nowDespite missing the earlier family gatherings, Sunita has found ways to enjoy the festival independently. She said she lights diyas at home and treats herself to sweets. However, she also has to be mindful of her food choices because of diabetes."Ab main akele hi apni khushiyan bana leti hoon. Ghar mein diye jalati hoon aur mithai khati hoon. Diabetes hai, isliye soch-samajhkar khati hoon, lekin apni Diwali enjoy karti hoon." ("Now, I create my own happiness on my own. I light diyas at home and eat sweets. I have diabetes, so I have to be careful about what I eat, but I still enjoy my Diwali.")Sunita Ahuja remembers her first Diwali after marrying GovindaSunita also revisited memories from the early years of her marriage. Recalling her first Diwali as Govinda's wife, she spoke about the gifts she received from her mother-in-law. According to Sunita, the actor has become somewhat miserly over the years. articles.title: Diwali 2026: 50+ Heartfelt Wishes, Greetings, Messages, and Quotes for the Festival of Lights
articles.summary: Ask ten people what Diwali means and you’ll get ten answers. For some it’s the smell of ghee and sugar drifting out of the kitchen.
articles.body: Ask ten people what Diwali means and you’ll get ten answers. For some it’s the smell of ghee and sugar drifting out of the kitchen. For others it’s the week of cleaning nobody enjoys, the rangoli that never comes out symmetrical, or the one relative who turns up every year with a box of mithai.The name Deepavali means “a row of lights,” and the stories behind it change depending on where you are in India. Many Hindus celebrate Lord Rama’s return to Ayodhya after fourteen years in exile, and his defeat of Ravana. In other regions the focus is Goddess Lakshmi and the hope of a prosperous year. Some communities remember Lord Krishna’s victory over Narakasura. Jains mark the day Lord Mahavira attained moksha, and Sikhs observe Bandi Chhor Divas.Whatever the story in your family, the habit is the same: people get in touch. A short, honest message often means more than a gift, so here are some you can borrow or bend into your own words.Longer Diwali wishes and messagesThese suit family, close friends and anyone you’d like to say a little more to.May this Diwali light up your home, and also the dreams you’ve been quietly carrying around. Wishing you happiness, courage and a good fresh start.Even the smallest diya pushes back the dark. Remember that when things feel heavy. Happy Diwali.Hope prosperity finds your home this year, peace settles in your heart, and kindness guides the decisions you make.Here’s to a year with fewer worries, closer relationships and plenty of reasons to get together. Happy Diwali 2026!May your home always have room for laughter, your table always have a little extra, and your hope never run out.Let’s use this festival to drop the old grudges and make room for new people in our lives. Have a lovely Diwali.May Goddess Lakshmi fill your home with abundance, and may you have the wisdom to know what actually matters.Every hard chapter ends eventually, and the next page is usually better. Wishing you strength and new opportunities this Diwali.I hope you get conversations that outlast the festivities and memories that stay long after the diyas burn out.May the sweetness of Diwali spread into the rest of your life: good health, people who love you, and some real quiet.May the work you’ve put in finally pay off, the dreams on your list turn into plans, and the plans actually happen.Wishing you happiness in places you didn’t expect to find it. The best things in life tend to be the simple ones.May the festival’s light show you possibilities where you only saw doubt. Here’s to a prosperous year.Hope your celebration has family around, old friends nearby and something new to look forward to.Light each lamp with a prayer for someone who needs hope, or healing, or just a reason to smile.May your success never cost you your peace, and may money and good health always travel together.This Diwali, I hope you find the courage to forgive, the sense to keep growing and the generosity to share what you have.May your home be somewhere happiness is welcome, differences are respected and love is never in short supply.May the best things reach you this year. Not only wealth and success, but time, health and people who matter.May the glow of the diyas stay with you all year. articles.body: Suriya's 'Scene' opened strongly at the box office on November 6, while Nayanthara's 'Mookuthi Amman 2' had a comparatively slower start. Both films arrived in theatres on Friday, setting up an interesting box office clash this Diwali. While 'Scene' attracted a larger audience on its opening day, 'Mookuthi Amman 2' registered a relatively modest start. The opening-day figures have set the stage for their first weekend performance.Suriya's 'Scene' crosses Rs 22 crore gross on Day 1According to Sacnilk, 'Scene' collected Rs 19.15 crore net in India on its opening day, taking its domestic gross collection to Rs 22.25 crore. The film recorded 6,167 shows across its Tamil and Telugu versions. The Tamil version contributed Rs 16.15 crore, while the Telugu version added Rs 3 crore.Meanwhile, 'Mookuthi Amman 2' earned Rs 1.88 crore net on Day 1, with its India gross collection standing at Rs 2.15 crore. Its Tamil version contributed Rs 1.75 crore, while the Telugu version added Rs 13 lakh.'Scene' vs 'Mookuthi Amman 2' box office collection Day 2 LiveOn Day 2, 'Scene' has collected an estimated Rs 4.88 crore net in India so far. The film has recorded 1,972 shows, with the Tamil version contributing Rs 4.07 crore from 1,557 shows. The Telugu version has added Rs 81 lakh through 415 shows. Its total India net collection has now reached Rs 24.03 crore, while its domestic gross collection stands at Rs 28.01 crore.On the other hand, 'Mookuthi Amman 2' has recorded an estimated Rs 53 lakh net in India on its second day. The film has registered 666 shows so far, with the Tamil version contributing Rs 49 lakh from 588 shows. The Telugu version has earned an additional Rs 4 lakh from 71 shows, while its Kannada collection is yet to be reported.The film's total India net collection currently stands at Rs 2.41 crore, while its domestic gross collection has reached Rs 2.78 crore. articles.title: Adivi Sesh says ‘the real luxury is having everyone you love under one roof’; reveals why he prefers lighting diyas over bursting crackers on Diwali
articles.summary: Actor Adivi Sesh has shared how his perspective on Diwali has changed with age, saying the festival is now more about spending quality time with loved
articles.body: Actor Adivi Sesh has shared how his perspective on Diwali has changed with age, saying the festival is now more about spending quality time with loved ones than indulging in grand celebrations. The ‘Dacoit’ actor also spoke about becoming more environmentally conscious, revealing that he prefers lighting diyas over bursting crackers because of their impact on animals and the environment.In a conversation with IANS, the actor spoke about how his approach to the festival has become more thoughtful as he has grown older. He said, “Definitely. When you're younger, Diwali is about everything happening around you. The lights, the celebrations, the excitement. As you grow older, it becomes more about the people around you.”Adivi Sesh calls family togetherness the real luxuryThe ‘Major’ actor also said that he has come to value having his loved ones together during the festival. He described spending time with family as the real luxury of Diwali.“I've realised that the real luxury is having everyone you love under one roof, happy and healthy. I think that's what festivals are meant to remind us of. Life gets busy, people move to different places, and you don't always get to spend as much time together as you'd like. So when you do, those moments become really precious,” he said.Actor recalls childhood Diwali celebrationsLooking back at his childhood, Adivi Sesh said Diwali was primarily about the excitement surrounding the festival. He recalled enjoying the holidays, sweets, new clothes and the festive atmosphere.“As kids, festivals were all about excitement. The holidays, the sweets, the new clothes, the whole atmosphere! You didn't really think about why everyone was celebrating. You just knew it was a happy time,” he said.Adivi Sesh prefers lighting diyas over bursting crackersThe actor also spoke about why he now prefers lighting diyas over bursting crackers, explaining how he has become more mindful of their impact on animals.“As you grow older, I think you become more conscious of how your celebrations affect the world around you. I'm much more environmentally conscious now, and I'm particularly sensitive to how loud crackers affect animals.”“Our pets get really disturbed by those sounds, and I know it's the same for so many animals outside. So today, I prefer lighting diyas and celebrating without all that noise. The excitement is still there, but I think the way I experience it has become a little more thoughtful,” Sesh added.Adivi Sesh's upcoming and recent projectsOn the work front, Adivi Sesh was last seen in the romantic action thriller ‘Dacoit’, co-starring Mrunal Thakur as the female lead. articles.title: Guru Randhawa to make EDC debut, premiere ‘Sirra’ remix with Steve Aoki
articles.summary: India, November 6, 2026: Punjabi pop star Guru Randhawa is set to take the global stage on November 7, becoming the first India-born artist to perform at
articles.body: India, November 6, 2026: Punjabi pop star Guru Randhawa is set to take the global stage on November 7, becoming the first India-born artist to perform at Electric Daisy Carnival (EDC), one of the world's biggest electronic dance music festivals. The performance will also mark his debut at an international music festival.Adding to the occasion, Randhawa will share the mainstage with two-time Grammy-nominated DJ and producer Steve Aoki for the world premiere of their collaborative remix of ‘Sirra’. The reworked version of the chart-topping track brings together Punjabi pop melodies and high-energy electronic dance music, marking a cross-genre collaboration aimed at international dance floors.The remix builds on the success of the original song, which featured on Randhawa's album ‘Without Prejudice’. The track has garnered 356 million cumulative streams and 550 million YouTube views, while making its presence felt across streaming charts and social media platforms.Randhawa's EDC appearance adds another milestone to his growing list of international collaborations. Over the years, he has worked with global names across genres, including Pitbull on the Billboard-charting ‘Slowly Slowly’, Tito El Bambino on the Spanish-Punjabi track ‘Mueve La Cintura’, French Montana on ‘Vibe’, Jay Sean on ‘Surma Surma’, K-pop group LE SSERAFIM on ‘BOOMPALA’, The Chainsmokers on ‘Addicted’ and Rick Ross on ‘Rich Life’.Speaking about the performance, Guru Randhawa said, “Representing India and our sound on the EDC mainstage is a massive honour. Steve Aoki and I have built something special with the 'Sirra' remix that completely fuses two very distinct worlds. Before our massive homecoming stadium show hits New Delhi, I can't wait to hit the EDC mainstage and unleash that 'Sirra' energy!”Steve Aoki added, “Electronic music is all about breaking boundaries and bridging cultures, so having Guru Randhawa join me on the EDC mainstage is incredible. I have some of my absolute fondest touring memories from India, and working on this 'Sirra' remix together has been an amazing experience. November 7th is going to be unforgettable.”The festival appearance will precede Randhawa's return to the Indian concert circuit with ‘Sirra Era Live in Concert’, scheduled for December 12 at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in New Delhi. The stadium show will mark his return to live touring after a three-year break and celebrate his 13 years in the music industry.The EDC set is expected to bring together Randhawa's signature Punjabi pop sound and Aoki's electronic music style, with the live debut of the remix serving as a preview of the singer's upcoming homecoming concert.The official ‘Sirra’ remix by Steve Aoki, facilitated by Warner Music India, is now available across major streaming platforms.You use AI every day.
